title: From CLIP to BLIP-2 — Q-Former as Modality Bridge

questions.question: With NUM_PATCH=64 and NUM_QUERY=8 in the toy, how many rows does cross_attention return?
options: 8, one attended output for each learnable query
64, because every patch becomes an output token
16, because QUERY_DIM is 16
24, because LLM_DIM controls the attention count
questions.explanation: Queries determine the output rows. The toy sends eight query vectors over 64 patch keys, so the attended result has eight rows.

questions.question: In cross_attention, which vectors provide Q, K, and V?
options: Q comes from patches and K/V both come from queries
Q comes from queries, while K and V come from the external patch features
All three projections come from the projected LLM output
Q, K, and V are all copied from the same patch row
questions.explanation: The implementation projects each query with W_q and each patch with W_k and W_v. That is cross-attention: the query slots ask for information from image features.

questions.question: What does top_patches_per_query(attn, k=3) return for each query?
options: The three smallest patch vectors by Euclidean norm
The three query rows with the highest entropy
The indices of the three patches with the largest attention weights
A single average patch shared by all queries
questions.explanation: For each attention row, the helper sorts patch indices by descending weight and keeps the first k indices. It reports likely evidence patches, not new embeddings.

questions.question: If W_out has shape 24x16 in linear_project, what is the shape of each projected query output?
options: 16 values, because the query dimension is preserved
64 values, because there are 64 input patches
8 values, because there are eight query slots
24 values, because each 16-dimensional attended query is mapped to LLM_DIM
questions.explanation: matmul_vec applies each of the 24 rows of W_out to a 16-dimensional attended vector. Every query therefore becomes one 24-dimensional LLM-facing token.

questions.question: Why should the first query in demo_biased attend most strongly to patch 5?
options: It is initialized from patches[5] and identity W_q/W_k makes that matching key strongest
Patch 5 is always the brightest patch in the random image
The softmax forces query 0 to choose the first five patches
The output projection hard-codes index 5 for every query
questions.explanation: The favored list starts with 5, and the query is copied from that patch. Identity projections preserve the match, so its dot product is expected to win.

questions.question: What is the architectural reason for using a small trainable Q-Former between frozen vision and language components?
options: It forces the LLM to process all 64 patches without compression
It learns a compact, task-directed bridge while avoiding the cost and instability of updating both large encoders
It replaces cross-attention with a fixed random lookup table
It makes image features discrete before the text decoder sees them
questions.explanation: The learnable queries compress many frozen patch features into a small set of projected tokens. This keeps most parameters frozen while the bridge learns the visual-to-language interface.
